ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $15.21 to the rider (per NS-7, voucher form, not cash) and record the driver's RD-1 breach of the shortest-and-most-direct-route obligation; no account flag (F16/F17 route upheld counts are 0, so the FD-6 repetition condition is not met).

segment_findings.reason: 6.94 km added between 21:46–21:56, up to 2240 m off the optimal route. The driver's accident claim (F11) is not made out under RD-4(a): although F14 places an accident on K-PLE at 0 m from the optimal route at 21:26, F13 shows that same expressway at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) during 21:27–22:24, i.e. flowing, and F12's band-4 record is on PIE, not the avoided stretch — the RD-4(b) corroboration is therefore absent (and in any case band ≤2 never counts alone, G3). No rider consent exists before 21:46 (F8–F10 are arrival messages only; F11 is a post-trip claim, not consent per RD-5/G11), and RD-3 does not apply. Segment is unexplained → RD-2.

3.85 km added between 22:04–22:13, up to 931 m off the optimal route. Same analysis as F3: no traffic record supports blockage of the replaced optimal stretch within this window (F13 shows band 5, F12 is a different road), and the chat contains no consent message before 22:04 (F8–F10). Unexplained → RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip claim of an unavoidable accident detour: the accident fact (F14) exists but the replaced road was recorded at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) in the trip window (F13), so no RD-4(a) exemption; a driver statement cannot substitute for rider consent (G11/RD-5).
PIE band-4 record does not corroborate the avoided stretch (K-PLE); band ≤2 is required for corroboration and a single band fact never exempts a segment (RD-4(b), G3).
